releaseNotes:
New: honest records for your models, the half markets on the board, and the closing line. Nothing you saved is changed.

Safety first
• Settings has "Safety copy" and "Restore". One file holds everything the app has collected; a copy is also put into Downloads. A copy is made by itself before this version first starts.
• After the update the app counts your games, receipts, models and codes and shows the count before and after.
• "New markets" in Settings switches the new reading, storing and showing off. What was stored stays.

A model's record counts only games it could not have known
• A model's record now starts when its formulas were last saved. Games older than that were already played when the formulas were written, so they prove nothing. The record over all games stays beside it.
• HOT, PROVEN and COLD need 100 results. Below that the badge says BUILDING. Your newest models lose their badge for now; that is the honest reading.
• All-Star weighs a model only by the games since its formulas were saved.

What a model is good at
• Each model's page has "Honest record and strengths": per market and per side (Over, Under, home, away), with the return at the bookmaker's price.
• A cell is called a strength only when it makes money and beats simply taking that side every time, by more than luck across all cells would give.

Half markets, and "Winner and total"
• Read from the bookmaker's board: first-half total, first-half handicap, second-half total, second-half handicap, and "Winner and total" with its four prices.
• Open a game's markets on the Matches tab: they are listed at the top with their lines, prices and what the bookmaker keeps, or "not offered". "Halves" shows every line.
• A saved game's page shows them as the board had them and, after the game, which side won, from the scores by half. Second-half results leave overtime out and say so.
• No model picks these yet. They get formulas in the next version.

The closing line
• Each time the app reads a game's board before tip-off it keeps every line and price in a file of its own. A later reading is kept beside the first, never in its place.
• Games about to tip off are read once more while the app is open, and during background checks if you have a watch or the morning brief set. "Read the board again now" on a game's page does it by hand.
• The game's page shows how each line moved. A model's page shows how often its side got a better number than the close.
• Settings, "Stored boards": how many games are stored and every market the bookmaker carries.

To do after updating
• Open Settings and look at the count under "Safety copy". If a number fell, delete nothing: use "Restore" with the copy made before the update.

New: AI Chat rebuilt. It sends far less with each request, answers sooner, reaches much more of the app, and can work while you are elsewhere.

Lighter and quicker
• "Hey" now sends a few hundred characters. Before, every message carried about 30,000.
• Only the tools a message needs go out with it. Large results stay on the phone and the AI reads the part it needs.
• The answer appears word by word, each step is named while it runs, and Stop ends it.
• A provider that is busy is tried again by itself. You can set a backup model in AI Chat settings. A run that failed is carried on with one tap, without fetching the same things again.

Games and lines
• NCAA men's games only, and the count matches the Matches tab.
• One scan reads the lines of every game on the list, so "every game with a handicap above 17.5" no longer stops at ten games.

More of the app
• The AI can now read governance, saved codes and how they ended, trials, training and captured games, switch a model on or off, set the Studio filters and more.
• A change to your models or settings still waits for your tap. A change to the Betslip runs at once and has an Undo button on its card.
• The AI can ask you a question with answers to tap, and can propose a plan of several changes for one approval. Minting and deleting are always asked one by one.

Chats and memory
• Up to 20 chats, each with a title. "New chat" keeps a long chat from slowing down.
• Quick commands under the message box (games today, my Betslip, model records and others) run with no AI request and no key.
• "Ask AI" on a game, a model, a saved code and the Betslip.
• Fast or Deep answers.
• The AI keeps up to 12 facts about how you bet. You read, change and delete them in AI Chat settings.

While you are away
• "Tell me when the handicap of Duke passes 17.5": a watch, told by a notification. Android checks about every 15 minutes at best, and battery saving can delay it.
• A morning brief written by the app itself, with no AI request. Off until you switch it on.
• A run goes on when you leave the app and notifies you at its end. Swiping the app away still ends it.

Measuring
• A tap on the line under an answer shows what every request behind it sent and received. Tokens are shown when the provider names them.
• AI Chat settings can test a model's tool use, keep a scoreboard per model, and run a fixed set of 38 requests with a result file to share.

After updating
• Allow notifications in AI Chat settings, under "Background work", if you want watches and the brief.
• The limits are unchanged: 12 AI requests and 20 tool calls per run, 120 and 240 per day. Reading the app's own data no longer counts as a tool call.
• Your chat from before the update is still there.

Good to know
• No pick, projection or record is calculated differently.
• This version was tested with made-up provider replies. It has not yet been tried against a live AI provider, so please report what goes wrong.

Fixed: the Betslip page now follows the Betslip at once.

What was wrong
• After a code was loaded, "Slip (x)" and the banner showed the games, but the game cards came much later.
• A removed game stayed on the page for a while. A swiped game left its red "Remove" background standing.
• A cleared Betslip kept its cards for a while.
The cause was one fault: the cards waited for every model card to be recalculated before they changed.

What is fixed
• Loaded games appear as soon as SportyBet has answered. Each card first shows the game, the market, the pick and the price with "Working out the model picks for this game…", and gets its model row a moment later.
• A game removed with ✕ leaves at once. "Undo" still follows.
• "Clear Slip" shows the empty Betslip at once.
• "Loading…" ends when the code is in the Betslip. It no longer waits for every model card.
• The record of the models against the bookmaker is now worked out once and kept while your saved games and models stay the same. Before, it was worked out again several times for every change to the Betslip. This is the largest part of the time saved.

Changed at your request
• Swipe-to-delete is removed. A game is removed with ✕ only.

Also
• Models and Decisions now show a line at the top while their picks are still being worked out for a changed Betslip. Until that line goes, the cards there are from the Betslip before its last change, so wait for it before you generate a code from them.
• A storage error while the Betslip is changed is now shown as a message. Before, it could close the app.

Good to know
• No pick, projection or record is calculated differently. The same calculations run, fewer times and after the page has changed.
• The time SportyBet takes to answer a code is not changed.

New: Governance beside All-Star. The Governance page has a new button, "Compare with All-Star". It opens a page that puts governance's pick and All-Star's pick side by side, game by game, and says why each picked what it picked.

What you see
• One card per game. Governance is on the left, All-Star on the right, each with its pick and its price.
• A mark on every card: Same pick, Same side other line, Other market, Opposite sides, Only governance, Only All-Star, or Neither.
• "Upcoming" shows the Betslip games that have not started, with the picks of this moment. "Played" shows the games past tip-off, as the picks were written before the game, with Won or Lost on each side once the score is in.
• Filters: All, They differ, They agree. The line above the cards counts the games of each mark.

"Show why" on a card
• Why governance picked it, and why All-Star picked it: how many models backed it, who led, its confidence and its verdict.
• How each voice sided in the market.
• Where the two differ: why governance did not take All-Star's pick, and where governance's market stood in All-Star's own ranking.
• When Line Comfort moved All-Star's line: its own line and the moved line.
• After the game: All-Star's side graded on the bookmaker's main line too. That keeps "who chose the better side" apart from "who chose the easier line".
• The models on trial. Governance listens to them. All-Star does not let them vote.

Scoreboard
• Wins and losses of both when they agreed, of both when they differed, and of each when only one picked.
• A return is quoted from 20 priced picks. Before that the numbers are too few to judge by.

A code from the agreed games
• "Make a code from the agreed games" books the upcoming games where both took the same market and side.
• It is booked on the bookmaker's main line, the line governance measures on. All-Star's own line can be another one.
• The code is saved in Codes under "Governance", named "Agreed with All-Star".
• Agreement has not been shown to win more. The scoreboard is where that will show over time.

Good to know
• Nothing about how governance or All-Star picks has changed. This page only shows and compares.
• All-Star here is the one of the Decisions tab, with the filters and the Line Comfort you set there.
• Games written into the journal before this update show All-Star's pick without its reason and without its ranking. Full cards start with games captured after the update.
• The page follows your pack level. At "Also strongest watching" governance's side is made of patterns that did not pass the rules.
• The governance report file now holds the comparison too.

New: a loading screen. When the app opens, it now shows a loading screen with a progress bar until your saved data is on the pages. Before, the pages opened at once and stood empty for a while, which looked as if your data was gone.

What you see
• A bar with the percentage, the step ("Step 6 of 8") and what is being done, for example "Reading your saved games: 412 of 1,300".
• The eight steps: models, team statistics, Betslip, saved codes, accuracy history, saved games, model picks, summaries.
• The pages open by themselves when everything is there.
• After 8 seconds a button "Open the app now" appears. The app then opens at once and the pages fill in as loading finishes.
• If you open the app that way, an empty Home or Results says "Still loading your saved games" until they are there. It no longer says that nothing is saved.

When it appears
• Every time the app starts from nothing: when you open it, and when Android closed it in the background and you come back to it.
• Not when you move between pages, and not when you return to the app while it is still running.

Good to know
• The loading is the same work as before. It is not faster. You now see how far it is and that nothing is missing.
• The app reads what is saved on the phone. Your saved data is not changed by it.
• With little or nothing saved, the screen is gone almost at once.
• If a loading step fails, the screen closes and the app says so, as before.
• Settings, "Share startup diagnostics": the report now says how long the load took (the line "first-load").

New: the result of every code. Results has a fourth tab, Codes, that shows how many games of each saved code won, which ones lost, and by how much.

What you see
• Each saved code as a card: the code, who made it, the tally ("7 of 10 won · 2 lost · 1 pending") and a verdict: Won, Lost, Lost by one game, Pending.
• Tap anywhere on a card and it opens where it is, with one row per game: the bet, the odds, the final score, Won or Lost, and how close it was ("Lost by 1.5 points"). Tap again and it closes.
• For a lost code: what it would have paid without the lost games.
• Filters: All, Won, Lost, Pending. Time: 7 days, 30 days, all time.
• Records, in one card you can open: by who made the code (each model, Governance, your own slips), by the number of games in the code, by bet type with the one that loses most often, and by the odds of the game.
• "Copy result" and "Share result" give the whole result as text.
• In Analyze, Codes: each saved code now has a line such as "7/10 Lost". Tap it to see its games in Results.

Where the results come from
• From Refresh Scores. The codes read the final scores that Refresh Scores already saves on the games in Results. No request is sent for a code.
• A code keeps a copy of its final scores, so its result stays when you later delete the games from Results. Deleting the code itself removes its result.

When a bet can't be checked
• The row says "Can't be checked yet" and gives the reason: no result is saved for the game (it is not in Results), the bet needs quarter scores that were not saved, or the app does not know the bet type.
• Winner, handicap, match total and each team's total are checked from the final score, overtime included. Quarter and half bets are checked when the quarter scores were saved.
• A score exactly on the line, or a cancelled game, is shown as Void: the bet leaves the code.

Good to know
• This is the app's own check of the score against the bet. The bookmaker's settlement decides.
• The newest 120 saved codes are shown.
• Governance codes are judged like every other code and appear beside the models in the records. Governance does not learn from these records.
• The tabs in Results now scroll sideways, because four do not fit on a narrow screen.

After updating
• Open Results and tap Refresh Scores once, then open the Codes tab.

New: Governance, a layer above the models. It is a sixth tab in Analyze, after Models. Nothing else in the app was changed.

What it is
• Governance has no formula. It keeps a small ledger of the side every enabled model took in every finished game, and measures patterns of agreement in it: one model against the majority, two or three models agreeing, and most models agreeing.
• It runs by itself, in the background, when the saved games or the models change and when its page opens. No train button, no AI, no quota.
• It keeps what it learned on the phone and carries on from it at every start.

How it judges a pattern
• By return per bet at the captured odds, never by win rate alone.
• A pattern is found in the older 70% of the games and must hold in the newest 30%, which the search does not look at. It must also beat each of its own members alone.
• A found pattern is on probation. It is confirmed only by games played after it was found: at least 8, with a return above zero by more than its uncertainty. If they return zero or less it is retired.
• The rules are fixed and shown on the page. Governance cannot change them.

What you can do with it
• Pack: its picks for the games in the Betslip, one per game, on the bookmaker's main line, each with its reason. "Generate code" books exactly the picks shown; the code is in Codes under the new Governance filter.
• Pack level: Confirmed only (the default), also On probation, also the strongest Watching. Games in a pack: 3, 5, 8, 10 or all.
• Its own record: it writes its pick down before tip-off and never rewrites it. The page shows that record beside All-Star's on the same games.
• Voices: models that take the same side in 85% of results count as one voice. The page lists them and the closest pairs of models.
• After a new model version the page says whether it is still the same voice. If not, its patterns stop and the version starts fresh.
• "Save governance report as JSON" gives one file with all of this and the ledger.
• The switch at the top turns governance off; what it learned is kept.

What to expect at first
• An empty pack at the default level, with the reason on the page. Confirming a pattern takes weeks of captured games.
• The widest pack level gives picks from the first day. They are marked "may be luck", and most of them are.
• Tested on made-up games before release: with models that have no skill, luck was confirmed in 4 runs of 100 over 1,500 games. A pair that is right 65% of the time when it agrees was confirmed in 92 runs of 100, after about 680 games; a pair that is right 58% in 8 of 100. Governance finds large effects and misses small ones.

Not in this update
• Pattern ideas from the AI. They come in 2.14.1, after the first governance report.

After updating
• Open Analyze, then Governance. The first run replays every saved game for every enabled model and can take a while.

Model training: the faults found in the LRSV training log of 14 November are fixed. Nothing else in the app was changed.

Fixed
• An AI answer is no longer thrown away because of one misplaced bracket. In that run the third answer held three shapes and was lost whole. Now the phone puts the brackets right, uses the shapes, and says so in the log.
• Returns are worked out only on bets that have captured odds. When SportyBet's price on a heavy favourite was too short to be captured, the app used to pay the win at an assumed 1.87. In that run this turned +8.4% per bet on the held-out games into +13.3%. Such a side still counts in the win–loss record; the log now says how many sides the return is worked out on.
• For your own models the AI no longer has to copy your formulas. It writes a short name for each one (for example base.matchTotal) and the phone puts the formula in. In the third answer of that run the AI mistyped a stat while copying a 430-character formula, in two of its three shapes.
• The AI is now shown all the projections your model has, not two. Before, it answered with two and left the others untouched, so its shapes lost to the phone's own re-fit every time.
• The home-win chance of your own model is now re-fitted with the other projections when the phone re-fits the numbers. Before, it was never touched.
• The AI is told what each stat means (most are season totals, not per-game figures) and which kind of blank belongs on a term it adds. When one of its shapes starts far from your model, the next request tells it so and why.
• Requests to the AI repeat far less: a formula is written once, not once for every shape that was tried. The third request of that run would have been about a third shorter.
• Wording: "stopped at the edge" now names the edge and says that the figure shown is after the pull toward neutral; "a offset" reads "an offset"; the list of practice games says where the rest are; an unreadable answer is no longer counted as a shape that was tried.

New
• The check "Holds up on the held-out games" now also says when the average leaning of a market moved further from the results. It is for your information and blocks nothing.

Unchanged
• Five checks, the same rules for going to trial, and the AI still never chooses a number. A version already on trial is not touched.
• The assessment of AI models still marks an answer with broken brackets as a fault of that model.

After updating
• Nothing to do. Returns in new training logs can read lower than in old logs of the same games: the old figure included the assumed price.

Fixed
• The code pop-up and the code buttons no longer wait once the code exists. Until now, after SportyBet had answered, the app first recalculated every model card, both All-Star cards, every decision card and the match list, and captured the Betslip again. Only then did it open the pop-up and release the buttons. That is why a code could already stand in the Codes tab while its own button still said "Working…".
• Now the pop-up opens and the code is on its card as soon as SportyBet has answered. The recalculation and the capture still happen, afterwards and in the background.
• This holds for every code button in Analyze: Betslip, Models, Decisions, All-Star, pods and "Generate all". In "Generate all" each card shows its code as it arrives and the queue goes straight on to the next model.
• Less is done before SportyBet is asked, too: the Betslip is no longer captured in front of the request, and the board of a game on a moved line is read once instead of twice.

Unchanged
• After a code appears the code buttons count down 3 seconds, as before.
• A code is made for exactly the picks on the card, and a moved line is still checked against a fresh SportyBet board before the code is made. That check and the code itself take as long as SportyBet takes to answer.

New
• Settings, "Share startup diagnostics": the report now lists how long each step around your last codes took, in milliseconds. If a code still feels slow, generate one, then share the report: it shows where the time went. It holds no picks and no codes.

Fixed
• A game that has not been played can no longer be saved as finished. SportyBet reported one game as "ended, 0–0" eleven hours before its tip-off, and the app took it as the result. A final score is now refused when it gives a team 0 points, or when it arrives before, or within an hour of, the tip-off.
• A game saved with such a score is repaired at the next score refresh: the false score is removed, the game waits again and gets its real score after it is played. The message after the refresh names every game this happened to.
• A trial counts a game only after its tip-off has passed. The game that was counted too early goes back to "waiting" as soon as you open the trial.
• When SportyBet keeps giving a false score for a game that has been played, ESPN is asked instead. This needs the results source "SportyBet + ESPN Backup" in Settings.

New
• Check for update now only checks. When a new version is found you see what it brings: the fixes and features of every version you do not have yet, with the date and the download size.
• The download starts when you tap "Download and install". When it is done the Android installer opens by itself, as before.
